ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two horizontal blue lines, labeled on the right as y and z respectively, and the two horizontal lines have the same double-arrow markings, indicating y ∥ z. The slanted line x intersects both y and z. At the intersection of x and y, ∠3 is located above the horizontal line y and on the left side of the slanted line x, and ∠4 is located above the horizontal line y and on the right side of the slanted line x. At the intersection of x and z, ∠12 is located above the horizontal line z and on the right side of the slanted line x. Reasoning: Because y ∥ z, and x is a transversal, the corresponding angles ∠4 and ∠12 are equal. Given m∠12 = 64, therefore m∠4 = 64. At the upper intersection, ∠3 and ∠4 form a pair of linear angles on line y, so the sum of their measures is 180. Thus m∠3 = 180 - 64 = 116.

raw_record.question_text: In the figure, $m \angle 12 = 64$. Find the measure of $\angle 3$.

method.method_draft: First read the diagram: the two horizontal lines labeled y and z have matching double arrow marks, so they are parallel. The slanted line x intersects both of them. Angle 12 is at the lower intersection with z, above z and to the right of x; angle 4 is in the corresponding position at the upper intersection with y. Since y ∥ z, corresponding angles formed by transversal x are congruent, so m∠4 = m∠12 = 64. At the top intersection, ∠3 and ∠4 form a linear pair on line y, so they sum to 180. Therefore m∠3 = 180 - 64 = 116.
